This field is set when the token is successfully used to reset a password, when it expires, or when it is explicitly revoked. For customer and administrator password resets, this provides an audit trail of token usage. For seller password resets, this field is null since the seller password reset table does not track invalidation separately.
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Aggregates with conditional null: maps deleted_at column from shopping_mall_customer_password_resets or shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets, or returns null for shopping_mall_seller_password_resets (seller table lacks this field). Set when the token is used successfully, expired, or explicitly revoked. Allows soft delete for audit trail while preventing reuse.

user_type.description:
Type of user account associated with this password reset token.

This field indicates whether the password reset belongs to a customer, seller, or administrator account. It is computed based on which password reset table contains the record and enables the API to return the appropriate user summary type in the user field.
user_type.x-autobe-specification: Computed field with no direct database mapping. Determined by which password reset table contains the record: 'customer' if found in shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, 'seller' if found in shopping_mall_seller_password_resets, or 'administrator' if found in shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets. This discriminator enables the user object to use the correct $ref type.

user.description:
Summary information of the user account associated with this password reset token.

This object contains the user's account details including email address, approval status (for sellers), grade (for administrators), and account timestamps. The structure varies based on user_type: customer summaries include profile information, seller summaries include approval status and shop details, and administrator summaries include privilege grade and ban status.
user.x-autobe-specification: Computed field with no direct database mapping. Based on user_type, performs a JOIN to the corresponding user table: shopping_mall_customers for 'customer', shopping_mall_sellers for 'seller', or shopping_mall_administrators for 'administrator'. Returns the ISummary schema of the appropriate user type containing email, status, and account information.

IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.description:
Unified password reset token record containing token details and associated user information for administrative oversight and security auditing.

This response type consolidates password reset data from customer, seller, and administrator accounts into a single structure for administrative viewing and security monitoring purposes. The password reset token is a one-time use credential generated when a user requests to recover their account access after forgetting their password.

The user_type field indicates which type of account (customer, seller, or administrator) the password reset belongs to, and the user object contains the associated user's summary information including their email and account status. The deleted_at field may be null for seller password resets since the seller password reset table does not include this field, while customer and administrator password reset tables track token invalidation.
IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregates password reset data from three separate tables: shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, shopping_mall_seller_password_resets, and shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets.

Query logic:
1. Accept resetId as UUID path parameter
2. Search across all three password reset tables to find matching record by id
3. Determine user_type based on which table contains the record (customer/seller/administrator)
4. Join with corresponding user table (shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_sellers, or shopping_mall_administrators) to fetch user summary information
5. Normalize field names: map seller's expires_at to expired_at for consistency across all user types
6. Handle deleted_at: include the value if it exists (customer/administrator tables), set to null if not (seller table lacks this field)
7. Return 404 if resetId is not found in any of the three tables

Field mapping:
- id: Direct mapping from the id column of whichever password reset table contains the record
- token: Direct mapping from the token column of the source password reset table
- created_at: Direct mapping from the created_at column of the source password reset table
- expired_at: From expired_at column (customer/administrator) or expires_at column (seller) with normalization
- deleted_at: From deleted_at column (customer/administrator) or null (seller table has no deleted_at field)
- user_type: Computed field set to 'customer', 'seller', or 'administrator' based on the source table
- user: $ref to the ISummary schema of the corresponding user type (customer/seller/administrator)

profile_type.description:
Filter profiles by type: customer or seller.

When specified, only profiles of the selected type are returned. When omitted, both customer and seller profiles are included in the search results. This enables administrators to focus their search on a specific user type or retrieve a combined view of all platform profiles.
profile_type.x-autobe-specification: Computed filter parameter that determines which profile table(s) to query. When set to 'customer', query shopping_mall_customer_profiles. When set to 'seller', query shopping_mall_seller_profiles. When not specified, query both tables and combine results. This parameter enables administrators to filter results by profile type for targeted searches.

search.description:
Search query string for finding profiles by name or email.

Performs a case-insensitive partial match search across display names, shop names, and email addresses. Enter any portion of a name or email to find matching profiles. Useful for quickly locating specific users when you know part of their identifying information.
search.x-autobe-specification: Computed search parameter that performs case-insensitive LIKE matching across multiple fields. For customer profiles, searches display_name and email fields from shopping_mall_customer_profiles and shopping_mall_customers. For seller profiles, searches shop_name, shop_description, and email fields from shopping_mall_seller_profiles and shopping_mall_sellers. Uses SQL LIKE with wildcards for partial matching.

approval_status.description:
Filter seller profiles by approval status: pending, approved, or rejected.

This filter applies only to seller profiles and has no effect when searching customer profiles. Use this to view sellers awaiting approval, active sellers on the platform, or sellers whose applications were denied. Helpful for administrators managing the seller approval workflow.
approval_status.x-autobe-specification: Computed filter parameter that applies only to seller profiles. Filters shopping_mall_seller_profiles by the approval_status column. Valid values are 'pending' (awaiting administrator approval), 'approved' (seller can operate on platform), or 'rejected' (application denied). When searching customer profiles or when this parameter is omitted, this filter has no effect.

is_suspended.description:
Filter profiles by suspension status.

When set to true, returns only profiles that are currently suspended. When set to false, returns only active profiles that are not suspended. When omitted, includes all profiles regardless of their suspension status. This helps administrators monitor suspended accounts or view only active users.
is_suspended.x-autobe-specification: Computed filter parameter that filters profiles by suspension status. For customer profiles, checks the banned flag in shopping_mall_customers. For seller profiles, checks the is_suspended flag in shopping_mall_seller_profiles. When set to true, returns only suspended/banned profiles. When set to false, returns only active (non-suspended) profiles. When omitted, includes all profiles regardless of suspension status.

is_banned.description:
Filter profiles by ban status.

When set to true, returns only profiles that are permanently banned from the platform. When set to false, returns only profiles that are not banned. When omitted, includes all profiles regardless of their ban status. This helps administrators review banned accounts or focus on active users.
is_banned.x-autobe-specification: Computed filter parameter that filters profiles by ban status. For customer profiles, checks the banned flag in shopping_mall_customers. For seller profiles, checks the is_banned flag in shopping_mall_seller_profiles. When set to true, returns only banned profiles. When set to false, returns only non-banned profiles. When omitted, includes all profiles regardless of ban status.

created_after.description:
Filter profiles created on or after this date-time.

Specify an ISO 8601 date-time string to include only profiles that were created at or after this moment. Useful for viewing recently registered users or analyzing user growth over specific time periods. Can be combined with created_before to define a date range.
created_after.x-autobe-specification: Computed filter parameter that applies a lower bound date filter on profile creation. Filters shopping_mall_customer_profiles or shopping_mall_seller_profiles by the created_at column using >= comparison. The value must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string. Profiles created on or after this timestamp are included in results.

created_before.description:
Filter profiles created before this date-time.

Specify an ISO 8601 date-time string to include only profiles that were created before this moment. Useful for viewing historical user data or analyzing user registrations within specific time periods. Can be combined with created_after to define a date range.
created_before.x-autobe-specification: Computed filter parameter that applies an upper bound date filter on profile creation. Filters shopping_mall_customer_profiles or shopping_mall_seller_profiles by the created_at column using < comparison. The value must be a valid ISO 8601 date-time string. Profiles created before this timestamp are included in results.

page.description:
Page number to retrieve (1-indexed).

Specifies which page of results to return, starting from page 1. Each page contains up to 'limit' number of profiles. Use this parameter to navigate through large result sets. The default is page 1 when this parameter is omitted.
page.x-autobe-specification: Computed pagination parameter that specifies which page of results to retrieve. Uses 1-indexed pagination (page 1 is the first page). The value must be a positive integer (minimum 1). Combined with the limit parameter to calculate the OFFSET in SQL queries. Default value is 1 when not specified.

limit.description:
Maximum number of profiles to return per page (1-100).

Controls how many profile records are included in each page of results. The minimum is 1 and the maximum is 100. Use a larger limit to retrieve more data per request, or a smaller limit for finer pagination control. The default is typically 20 profiles per page.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Computed pagination parameter that specifies the maximum number of profiles to return per page. The value must be a positive integer between 1 and 100 (inclusive). Used as the LIMIT clause in SQL queries. Default value is typically 20 or similar when not specified. Maximum is capped at 100 to prevent excessive data retrieval.

IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and listing customer and seller profiles on the shopping mall platform.

This request object supports filtering profiles by type (customer or seller), searching by name or email, filtering by approval and suspension status, and applying date range filters. Results are returned in paginated format with configurable page size. Used by administrators to search for specific profiles, generate reports, and monitor platform user activity.
IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Computed request DTO for profile search across shopping_mall_customer_profiles and shopping_mall_seller_profiles tables. The profile_type filter determines which table(s) to query. The search parameter performs LIKE matching on display_name (customer), shop_name (seller), and email fields. The approval_status filter applies only to seller profiles (pending/approved/rejected). The is_suspended and is_banned filters check the corresponding boolean flags in the profile tables. The created_after and created_before filters apply date range constraints on the created_at timestamp. Pagination is handled by page (1-indexed) and limit (1-100) parameters. Results are combined from both tables and returned as IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.ISummary objects with a profile_type discriminator.

profile_type.description:
Type discriminator identifying whether this profile represents a customer or seller account.

This field distinguishes between the two profile types in the union schema. Value is 'customer' for customer profiles or 'seller' for seller profiles. Used by API consumers to determine which profile-specific fields are present in the response and how to interpret the data.
profile_type.x-autobe-specification: Computed discriminator field. Set to 'customer' when data originates from shopping_mall_customer_profiles joined with shopping_mall_customers, or 'seller' when data originates from shopping_mall_seller_profiles joined with shopping_mall_sellers. Used as discriminator for oneOf union type to distinguish between customer and seller profile variants in the response.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the profile record.

Universally Unique Identifier (UUID) that uniquely identifies this profile within the system. This field is immutable and serves as the primary key for the profile table (either customer_profiles or seller_profiles depending on profile_type). Used to reference the profile in other API operations.
id.x-autobe-specification: Primary key identifier from the respective profile table. For customer profiles: mapping from shopping_mall_customer_profiles.id. For seller profiles: mapping from shopping_mall_seller_profiles.id. UUID format, immutable after creation. Retrieved from the respective profile table based on profile_type discriminator in the UNION query.

email.description:
Email address associated with the user account.

The unique email address used for authentication and account identification. This field is populated from the linked customer or seller account (depending on profile_type) and serves as the primary login credential. Email addresses are unique across all user accounts in the system and are used for sending notifications and password reset links.
email.x-autobe-specification: Email address from joined actor table. For customer profiles: mapping from shopping_mall_customers.email via LEFT JOIN on customer_profiles.shopping_mall_customer_id = customers.id. For seller profiles: mapping from shopping_mall_sellers.email via LEFT JOIN on seller_profiles.seller_id = sellers.id. Unique constraint enforced at actor table level. Used for authentication and account identification.

created_at.description:
Timestamp indicating when the profile was created.

ISO 8601 formatted date-time string in UTC timezone representing the moment when this profile record was initially created in the system. This field is server-generated and immutable, providing an audit trail for profile creation and account age calculations.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Creation timestamp from the respective profile table. For customer profiles: mapping from shopping_mall_customer_profiles.created_at. For seller profiles: mapping from shopping_mall_seller_profiles.created_at. ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC timezone. Server-generated on profile creation during user registration, immutable after initial creation.

display_name.description:
Display name for customer profiles.

A user-friendly name displayed in place of or alongside the email address for customer accounts. This field is only applicable to customer profiles (profile_type='customer'). For seller profiles, the shop_name field is used instead. Customers can update this field to their preferred display name, which appears in order confirmations, shipping labels, and review author attribution.
display_name.x-autobe-specification: Customer profile display name. Mapping from shopping_mall_customer_profiles.display_name. Only present for customer profiles (profile_type='customer'). For seller profiles, this field is not applicable and will be null or omitted from the response. User-provided field that can be updated by the customer at any time.

phone_number.description:
Optional phone number for customer profiles.

Contact phone number for customer accounts, used for order notifications and seller communication regarding shipping issues or order clarifications. This field is only applicable to customer profiles (profile_type='customer') and is optional - customers may choose not to provide a phone number. For seller profiles, this field is not present.
phone_number.x-autobe-specification: Customer profile phone number. Mapping from shopping_mall_customer_profiles.phone_number. Only present for customer profiles (profile_type='customer'). Nullable field - customers may choose not to provide a phone number. For seller profiles, this field is not applicable and will be null or omitted from the response.

shop_name.description:
Shop name for seller profiles.

The business or shop name displayed for seller accounts on the platform. This field is only applicable to seller profiles (profile_type='seller') and is required for seller registration. The shop name is visible to customers browsing products and is used in order communications. For customer profiles, this field is not present.
shop_name.x-autobe-specification: Seller profile shop name. Mapping from shopping_mall_seller_profiles.shop_name. Only present for seller profiles (profile_type='seller'). Required field for seller profiles during registration. For customer profiles, this field is not applicable and will be null or omitted from the response. User-provided field that can be updated by the seller.

logo_uri.description:
Optional logo image URI for seller profiles.

Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) pointing to the seller's shop logo image. This field is only applicable to seller profiles (profile_type='seller') and is optional - sellers may choose not to upload a logo. The logo is displayed on the seller's shop page and in product listings. For customer profiles, this field is not present.
logo_uri.x-autobe-specification: Seller profile logo URI. Mapping from shopping_mall_seller_profiles.logo_uri. Only present for seller profiles (profile_type='seller'). Nullable field - sellers may choose not to upload a logo. URI format pointing to uploaded image file stored in the platform's file storage. For customer profiles, this field is not applicable and will be null or omitted from the response.

approval_status.description:
Approval status for seller profiles.

Current approval state of the seller's registration request. This field is only applicable to seller profiles (profile_type='seller') and can have values: 'pending' (awaiting administrator review), 'approved' (seller can list products), or 'rejected' (registration denied, may reapply). For customer profiles, this field is not present as customer accounts are immediately active upon registration.
approval_status.x-autobe-specification: Seller profile approval status. Mapping from shopping_mall_seller_profiles.approval_status. Only present for seller profiles (profile_type='seller'). Enumerated field with values: 'pending' (awaiting administrator review), 'approved' (seller can list products), or 'rejected' (registration denied, may reapply). For customer profiles, this field is not applicable as customer accounts are immediately active upon registration, and will be null or omitted from the response. Updated by administrators during seller approval process.

is_suspended.description:
Suspension status for seller profiles.

Boolean flag indicating whether the seller account is temporarily suspended. This field is only applicable to seller profiles (profile_type='seller'). When true, the seller cannot list new products or fulfill orders but retains access to view their account. Suspension is temporary and can be lifted by administrators. For customer profiles, this field is not present.
is_suspended.x-autobe-specification: Seller profile suspension flag. Mapping from shopping_mall_seller_profiles.is_suspended. Only present for seller profiles (profile_type='seller'). Boolean field indicating temporary account suspension. When true, the seller cannot list new products or fulfill orders but retains access to view their account. For customer profiles, this field is not applicable and will be null or omitted from the response. Updated by administrators.

is_banned.description:
Ban status for the user account.

Boolean flag indicating whether the account is permanently banned from the platform. This field applies to both customer and seller profiles. When true, the user cannot authenticate or access any platform features. Banned accounts retain their data for audit purposes but are completely inaccessible to the user. Ban actions are performed by administrators and are permanent.
is_banned.x-autobe-specification: Account ban status from joined actor table. For customer profiles: mapping from shopping_mall_customers.banned via LEFT JOIN on customer_profiles.shopping_mall_customer_id = customers.id. For seller profiles: mapping from shopping_mall_sellers.banned via LEFT JOIN on seller_profiles.seller_id = sellers.id. Boolean field indicating permanent account ban. When true, user cannot authenticate or access the platform. Applies to both customer and seller profiles. Updated by administrators.

IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of customer or seller profiles for administrative listing and search results.

This computed type provides essential profile information for either customers or sellers in a unified format. The profile_type field distinguishes between the two profile types, with each type having its own applicable fields.

Customer profiles include: id, email, display_name, optional phone_number, created_at, and banned status. Seller profiles include: id, email, shop_name, optional logo_uri, approval_status, suspension status, banned status, and created_at.

Used in paginated list responses for administrative oversight, profile search, and cross-user reporting functions.
IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Computed union type combining shopping_mall_customer_profiles and shopping_mall_seller_profiles with LEFT JOINs to their respective actor tables (shopping_mall_customers and shopping_mall_sellers). Query uses UNION of two result sets: (1) Customer profiles joined with customers table for email and banned status, (2) Seller profiles joined with sellers table for email and banned status. Each result set includes a profile_type discriminator field ('customer' or 'seller'). The oneOf schema discriminator on profile_type field distinguishes between the two profile variants. Filter results based on IShoppingMallCustomerProfile.IRequest search criteria. Apply pagination. Exclude soft-deleted profiles (deleted_at IS NULL) unless explicitly requested for audit purposes.

user_type.description:
User type filter for password reset records.

Restricts search results to a specific actor type. Choose from 'customer' for customer accounts, 'seller' for seller accounts, or 'administrator' for administrator accounts. This parameter determines which password reset table is queried.
user_type.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter to filter password reset records by user type. Maps to the source table: 'customer' filters shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, 'seller' filters shopping_mall_seller_password_resets, 'administrator' filters shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets. Determines which password reset table is queried and which user table is joined for email retrieval.

email.description:
Email address search filter for password reset records.

Searches for password reset requests associated with a specific email address. Performs a case-insensitive partial match on the email field. Useful for locating all password reset activity for a particular user account.
email.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter to search password reset records by user email address. Performs LIKE search on the email column from the joined user table (shopping_mall_customers.email, shopping_mall_sellers.email, or shopping_mall_administrators.email depending on user_type filter). Case-insensitive partial match.

status.description:
Status filter for password reset token state.

Filters results by the current state of the password reset token. 'active' shows valid, unused tokens that haven't expired. 'expired' shows tokens past their expiration time. 'used' shows tokens that have already been consumed for password reset.
status.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter to filter password reset records by token status. Computed from database columns: 'active' when deleted_at IS NULL AND expired_at > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'expired' when deleted_at IS NULL AND expired_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'used' when deleted_at IS NOT NULL.

date_range.description:
Date range filter for password reset record creation time.

Limits results to password reset requests created within a specific time period. Specify 'start' for the beginning of the range and 'end' for the end of the range. Both values must be in ISO 8601 date-time format. Either or both can be omitted for open-ended ranges.
date_range.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter to filter password reset records by creation date range. Applies WHERE clause: created_at BETWEEN date_range.start AND date_range.end. Both start and end are optional; if only one is provided, filters from start to infinity or from negative infinity to end.

page.description:
Page number for paginated results.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve. Page numbering starts from 1 (not 0). For example, page 1 returns the first set of results, page 2 returns the second set, and so on. The number of records per page is controlled by the pageSize parameter.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination parameter for page number. 1-indexed (first page is 1). Used in OFFSET calculation: OFFSET = (page - 1) * pageSize. Minimum value is 1.

pageSize.description:
Number of records per page.

Controls how many password reset records are returned in each page of results. Accepts values from 1 to 100. If not specified, defaults to 100 records per page. Larger page sizes may improve performance but increase response size.
pageSize.x-autobe-specification: Pagination parameter for records per page. Controls LIMIT clause in SQL query. Minimum value is 1, maximum value is 100. If omitted, defaults to 100 records per page.

sortBy.description:
Field name for sorting results.

Specifies which field to use for ordering the password reset records. Common options include 'created_at' to sort by creation time, 'user_email' to sort alphabetically by email, or 'id' for UUID-based ordering. If not specified, results default to sorting by creation date.
sortBy.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for sorting field name. Maps to ORDER BY clause column name. Valid values include: 'id', 'user_type', 'user_email', 'created_at', 'expired_at', 'status', 'deleted_at'. If omitted, defaults to 'created_at'.

sortOrder.description:
Sort direction for ordered results.

Determines whether results are sorted in ascending or descending order. 'asc' sorts from oldest to newest, or A to Z. 'desc' sorts from newest to oldest, or Z to A. If not specified, defaults to descending order (newest records first).
sortOrder.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for sort direction. Maps to ORDER BY ASC or DESC. 'asc' for ascending order (oldest first, A-Z), 'desc' for descending order (newest first, Z-A). If omitted, defaults to 'desc'.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records to return (deprecated).

Legacy parameter for controlling result count. This field is deprecated in favor of pageSize and may be removed in future API versions. If both limit and pageSize are provided, pageSize takes precedence. Defaults to 100 records if neither parameter is specified.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Deprecated pagination parameter. Previously used to limit maximum records returned. Now superseded by pageSize parameter. If both are provided, pageSize takes precedence. Defaults to 100 if neither is specified.

IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.IRequ.description:
Search criteria for filtering password reset requests across all user types in the shopping mall platform.

This request body enables administrators to search and filter password reset records by user type, email address, status, and date range. Results can be paginated and sorted according to specified parameters.

**Filtering Options**:

- **user_type**: Restrict results to a specific user type ('customer', 'seller', or 'administrator')
- **email**: Search for password resets associated with a specific email address
- **status**: Filter by reset token status ('active' for valid tokens, 'expired' for past tokens, 'used' for consumed tokens)
- **date_range**: Limit results to a specific time period using start and end dates

**Pagination**:

- **page**: Page number to retrieve (starts from 1)
- **pageSize**: Number of results per page (1-100)
- **sortBy**: Field name to sort results by
- **sortOrder**: Sort direction ('asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending)
IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.IRequ.x-autobe-specification:
Request body for searching and filtering password reset records across three source tables: shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, shopping_mall_seller_password_resets, and shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets.

Filter mappings:
- user_type: restricts results to specific actor type ('customer', 'seller', or 'administrator'), determining which password reset table is queried
- email: performs LIKE search on email field from joined user tables (shopping_mall_customers.email, shopping_mall_sellers.email, or shopping_mall_administrators.email)
- status: computed filter based on expired_at and deleted_at columns
  - 'active': deleted_at IS NULL AND expired_at > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  - 'expired': deleted_at IS NULL AND expired_at <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
  - 'used': deleted_at IS NOT NULL
- date_range: filters created_at column BETWEEN start AND end values

Pagination:
- page: page number (1-indexed, minimum 1)
- pageSize: records per page (minimum 1, maximum 100)
- sortBy: field name for ORDER BY clause
- sortOrder: 'asc' or 'desc' for sorting direction
- limit: deprecated, use pageSize instead

All fields are optional to allow flexible filtering combinations. Results are aggregated from all three password reset tables with user information joined from respective user tables.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the guest session.

This UUID identifies a specific guest session on the platform. It is used to reference the session in API operations and for tracking guest activity across the system.
id.x-autobe-specification: Mapped from shopping_mall_guest_sessions.id column. UUID format unique identifier for each guest session record.

actorType.description:
Type of actor associated with this session.

This field is always 'guest' for IShoppingMallGuestSession.ISummary, indicating the session belongs to an unauthenticated guest user identified by device fingerprint.
actorType.x-autobe-specification: Computed constant field set to 'guest' for all records from shopping_mall_guest_sessions table. This discriminator identifies the session as belonging to a guest actor type.

actorId.description:
Unique identifier of the guest account that owns this session.

This UUID references the guest account (identified by device fingerprint) associated with the session. It can be used to look up the guest's details or filter sessions by specific guest.
actorId.x-autobe-specification: Mapped from shopping_mall_guests_id foreign key column in shopping_mall_guest_sessions table. UUID format reference to the guest account record in shopping_mall_guests table.

actorEmail.description:
Email address of the actor associated with this session.

This field is always null for guest sessions since guest accounts do not have registered email addresses. Guests are identified by device fingerprint rather than email-based authentication.
actorEmail.x-autobe-specification: Computed field set to null for all guest sessions since guest accounts do not have email addresses. Guest users are identified by device fingerprint only, not by email credentials.

ip.description:
IP address from which the guest session was created.

This field contains the client IP address captured when the guest session was established. It is used for security monitoring, rate limiting, and detecting suspicious activity patterns.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Mapped from shopping_mall_guest_sessions.ip column. Captures the client IP address at session creation time. String format, may be IPv4 or IPv6 address.

href.description:
URL of the page where the guest session originated.

This field tracks the entry point for the guest session, showing which page the guest was on when they first accessed the platform. Used for session context and analytics.
href.x-autobe-specification: Mapped from shopping_mall_guest_sessions.href column. Captures the URL of the page where the guest session was initiated. String format.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest session was created.

This field records the exact date and time when the guest session was established. Used for calculating session age, expiration tracking, and audit trail purposes.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Mapped from shopping_mall_guest_sessions.created_at column. DateTime in ISO 8601 format with timezone. Automatically set when guest session is created.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the guest session expires.

This field indicates when the guest session becomes invalid. Sessions with an expired_at time in the past are considered expired. Used for automatic session invalidation and computing the status field.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Mapped from shopping_mall_guest_sessions.expired_at column. DateTime in ISO 8601 format with timezone. Set to a future time upon session creation based on session timeout period.

status.description:
Current status of the guest session.

This field indicates whether the session is currently active or has expired. 'active' means the session is still valid (expired_at is in the future). 'expired' means the session has timed out (expired_at is in the past).
status.x-autobe-specification: Computed field based on comparison of expired_at with current timestamp. Set to 'active' if expired_at > NOW(), 'expired' if expired_at <= NOW(). Evaluated at query time, not stored in database.

IShoppingMallGuestSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a guest session on the shopping mall platform.

This type provides session metadata for unauthenticated guest users identified by device fingerprint. It includes the session identifier, IP address, entry page URL, session lifecycle timestamps, and current status. The actorType is always 'guest' for this specific type.

Used for administrative oversight operations where administrators need to view and monitor guest sessions across the platform.
IShoppingMallGuestSession.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: Aggregates session data from shopping_mall_guest_sessions table for guest actor sessions. Maps id from shopping_mall_guest_sessions.id column. Computes actorType as constant 'guest'. Maps actorId from shopping_mall_guests_id foreign key column. Sets actorEmail to null since guest accounts have no email. Maps ip, href, created_at, expired_at directly from respective columns. Computes status by comparing expired_at with current timestamp: 'active' if expired_at > NOW(), 'expired' otherwise.

sessionType.description:
Discriminator field indicating the type of session (guest, customer, seller, or administrator).

This field helps API clients understand which type of user session is being returned, allowing them to handle the response data appropriately. The value is computed based on which session table the record was retrieved from.
sessionType.x-autobe-specification: Computed discriminator field indicating the session type. Value is determined by which session table the record was found in: 'guest' (shopping_mall_guest_sessions), 'customer' (shopping_mall_customer_sessions), 'seller' (shopping_mall_seller_sessions), or 'administrator' (shopping_mall_administrator_sessions). This field allows API consumers to handle different session types appropriately.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the session.

This UUID uniquely identifies the session across all session types. It is used to retrieve specific session details and track session lifecycle events.
id.x-autobe-specification: Primary key of the session record from the respective session table. For guest sessions: shopping_mall_guest_sessions.id. For customer sessions: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.id. For seller sessions: shopping_mall_seller_sessions.id. For administrator sessions: shopping_mall_administrator_sessions.id. This UUID uniquely identifies the session across all session tables.

userId.description:
Unique identifier of the user account associated with this session.

This field contains the UUID of the user (guest, customer, seller, or administrator) who owns this session. For guest sessions, this is the device fingerprint identifier.
userId.x-autobe-specification: Foreign key reference to the user account that owns this session. For guest sessions: shopping_mall_guests_id (references shopping_mall_guests.id). For customer sessions: shopping_mall_customer_id (references shopping_mall_customers.id). For seller sessions: shopping_mall_seller_id (references shopping_mall_sellers.id). For administrator sessions: shopping_mall_administrator_id (references shopping_mall_administrators.id).

userEmail.description:
Email address or device fingerprint of the user associated with this session.

For authenticated users (customer, seller, administrator), this contains their email address. For guest sessions, this contains the device fingerprint identifier since guests do not have email addresses.
userEmail.x-autobe-specification: Email address from the respective user table via JOIN. For customer sessions: shopping_mall_customers.email. For seller sessions: shopping_mall_sellers.email. For administrator sessions: shopping_mall_administrators.email. For guest sessions: shopping_mall_guests.device_fingerprint (guests do not have email addresses, so device fingerprint is used instead).

ip.description:
IP address from which the user logged in to create this session.

This field captures the client's IP address at the time of authentication. It is used for security monitoring, fraud detection, and identifying suspicious login patterns or unauthorized access attempts.
ip.x-autobe-specification: IP address from the respective session table. For guest sessions: shopping_mall_guest_sessions.ip. For customer sessions: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.ip. For seller sessions: shopping_mall_seller_sessions.ip. For administrator sessions: shopping_mall_administrator_sessions.ip. This is the IPv4 address from which the user logged in, captured at session creation time for security auditing.

href.description:
URL of the page where the user initiated the login request.

This field tracks the entry point for session creation. It is used for session context tracking and security analysis to understand how users access the platform.
href.x-autobe-specification: URL from the respective session table. For guest sessions: shopping_mall_guest_sessions.href. For customer sessions: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.href. For seller sessions: shopping_mall_seller_sessions.href. For administrator sessions: shopping_mall_administrator_sessions.href. This is the URL where the login request originated, captured for session context and security auditing.

referrer.description:
URL of the referring page that directed the user to the login page.

This field captures the source of user traffic for analytics and session context. It may be null if the user navigated directly to the login page without a referrer.
referrer.x-autobe-specification: HTTP referrer from the respective session table. For guest sessions: shopping_mall_guest_sessions.referrer. For customer sessions: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.referrer. For seller sessions: shopping_mall_seller_sessions.referrer. For administrator sessions: shopping_mall_administrator_sessions.referrer. Nullable - may be null if the user navigated directly to the login page.

createdAt.description:
Timestamp when this session was created (login time).

This field records the exact time when the user successfully authenticated and the session was established. It is used for session age calculation, expiration tracking, and audit trail purposes.
createdAt.x-autobe-specification: Creation timestamp from the respective session table. For guest sessions: shopping_mall_guest_sessions.created_at. For customer sessions: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.created_at. For seller sessions: shopping_mall_seller_sessions.created_at. For administrator sessions: shopping_mall_administrator_sessions.created_at. This timestamp records when the session was created (login time) and is used to calculate session age and for audit trail purposes.

expiredAt.description:
Timestamp when this session expires or was logged out.

This field indicates the absolute expiration time for the session. Sessions are automatically invalidated after this time regardless of logout status. It is used for automatic session cleanup and validity checking.
expiredAt.x-autobe-specification: Expiration timestamp from the respective session table. For guest sessions: shopping_mall_guest_sessions.expired_at. For customer sessions: shopping_mall_customer_sessions.expired_at. For seller sessions: shopping_mall_seller_sessions.expired_at. For administrator sessions: shopping_mall_administrator_sessions.expired_at. This timestamp indicates when the session expires or was logged out. Sessions with expired_at before current time are considered invalid.

IShoppingMallGuestSession.description:
Session details for any user type (guest, customer, seller, or administrator) including authentication metadata, client information, and associated user account data.

This response type is used by administrators to inspect session details for security monitoring and audit purposes. The sessionType discriminator field indicates which type of session this is, allowing clients to handle different session structures appropriately.

Session information includes the user's unique identifier, email address, IP address at login, referral source, creation time, and expiration status. This data helps administrators track user activity, detect suspicious login patterns, and investigate security incidents.
IShoppingMallGuestSession.x-autobe-specification: Union type aggregating session data from multiple session tables: shopping_mall_guest_sessions, shopping_mall_customer_sessions, shopping_mall_seller_sessions, and shopping_mall_administrator_sessions. Each session record is queried and joined with its respective user table (shopping_mall_guests, shopping_mall_customers, shopping_mall_sellers, shopping_mall_administrators) to retrieve user details. The sessionType discriminator field indicates which session table the data originated from. Business rule: Only authenticated administrators can access this endpoint for security monitoring and audit purposes. The endpoint queries all session tables to find the matching session ID, then performs the appropriate JOIN based on the session type found.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the password reset token record.

This UUID identifies the specific password reset request across all user types in the shopping mall platform. The ID is sourced from the respective password reset table based on the user_type.
id.x-autobe-specification: Primary key from one of three source tables: shopping_mall_customer_password_resets.id, shopping_mall_seller_password_resets.id, or shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets.id. Each table has UUID primary key.

user_type.description:
Type of user account that requested the password reset.

This field indicates which user type the password reset belongs to: 'customer' for shopper accounts, 'seller' for merchant accounts, or 'administrator' for platform administrator accounts.
user_type.x-autobe-specification: Computed field indicating the source table. Returns 'customer' if record from shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, 'seller' if from shopping_mall_seller_password_resets, or 'administrator' if from shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets.

user_email.description:
Email address of the user account requesting password reset.

This is the registered email address where the password reset token was sent. Used for administrative monitoring and audit purposes.
user_email.x-autobe-specification: Email address retrieved via JOIN to the respective user table. From customer.email if user_type is 'customer', seller.email if 'seller', or administrator.email if 'administrator'.

token.description:
Password reset token (masked for security).

This is the unique token sent to the user's email for password recovery. The token is masked in this view to prevent exposure of the full token value while still allowing administrators to identify and track reset requests.
token.x-autobe-specification: Password reset token from source table (customer, seller, or administrator password_resets table). Token is masked for security - only first 4 characters visible followed by '***'.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset request was created.

This indicates when the user requested a password reset and the token was generated and sent to their email address.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Timestamp from source table indicating when the password reset token was generated. All three source tables have created_at column with DateTime type.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token expires.

Tokens are time-limited for security. Once this time is reached, the token can no longer be used to reset the password and a new reset request must be made.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Expiration timestamp from source table. Normalized from expires_at column in seller table to expired_at in response. Customer and administrator tables use expired_at directly.

status.description:
Current status of the password reset token.

Possible values: 'active' (valid and unused), 'expired' (past expiration time), or 'used' (already consumed for password reset).
status.x-autobe-specification: Computed field based on deleted_at and expired_at. Returns 'active' if deleted_at is null AND expired_at > now, 'expired' if deleted_at is null AND expired_at <= now, 'used' if deleted_at is not null.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token was used or invalidated.

This field is set when the token is successfully used to reset a password, or when it is explicitly revoked. Null indicates the token is still valid (not yet used or expired).
deleted_at.x-autobe-specification: Soft delete timestamp from source table. Customer and administrator tables have deleted_at (nullable). Seller table lacks this column, treated as null for seller records. Indicates when token was used or invalidated.

IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.ISumm.description:
Summary view of a password reset request for administrative monitoring and security auditing.

This type represents a password reset token record from any user type (customer, seller, or administrator) in the shopping mall platform. It provides administrators with visibility into password reset activity across all user accounts for security monitoring and audit purposes.

The user_type field indicates which type of account requested the reset. The status field shows whether the token is active (valid and unused), expired (past expiration time), or used (already consumed). The token value is masked for security, showing only the first few characters to prevent exposure while still allowing administrators to identify and track reset requests.
IShoppingMallCustomerPasswordReset.ISumm.x-autobe-specification:
Aggregates password reset records from three source tables: shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, shopping_mall_seller_password_resets, and shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets.

JOINs:
- shopping_mall_customers via shopping_mall_customer_id to retrieve user_email for customer records
- shopping_mall_sellers via shopping_mall_seller_id to retrieve user_email for seller records
- shopping_mall_administrators via shopping_mall_administrator_id to retrieve user_email for administrator records

Computed fields:
- user_type: Returns 'customer' if from shopping_mall_customer_password_resets, 'seller' if from shopping_mall_seller_password_resets, or 'administrator' if from shopping_mall_administrator_password_resets
- status: Returns 'active' if deleted_at is null AND expired_at > now, 'expired' if deleted_at is null AND expired_at <= now, 'used' if deleted_at is not null
- token: Masked for security (first 4 characters + '***')

Field normalization:
- seller table uses 'expires_at' column, normalized to 'expired_at' in response
- seller table lacks 'deleted_at' column, treated as null for seller records
- All source tables have UUID primary keys, DateTime timestamps

actorType.description:
Actor type filter for session search.

Specifies which type of user's sessions to retrieve. Valid values are 'customer', 'seller', 'administrator', or 'guest'. If omitted, sessions from all actor types are included in the results. This parameter helps narrow down the search to a specific user type when managing sessions.
actorType.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter to filter sessions by actor type. Determines which session table to query: 'customer' -> shopping_mall_customer_sessions, 'seller' -> shopping_mall_seller_sessions, 'administrator' -> shopping_mall_administrator_sessions, 'guest' -> shopping_mall_guest_sessions. If not provided, queries all session tables with UNION ALL.

status.description:
Session status filter for active or expired sessions.

Filters sessions based on whether they are still valid or have expired. 'active' returns sessions where the expiration time is in the future, while 'expired' returns sessions where the expiration time is in the past. This is a computed field based on the expired_at timestamp compared to the current time.
status.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter to filter sessions by status. Computed by comparing expired_at timestamp with current time: 'active' means expired_at > NOW(), 'expired' means expired_at <= NOW(). Applied as a WHERE clause filter after querying session tables.

ip.description:
IP address filter for session search.

Filters sessions by the IP address from which the user logged in. Supports partial matching, so you can search for sessions from a specific IP or IP range. For example, entering '192.168.1' will match all sessions from IP addresses starting with that prefix.
ip.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter to filter sessions by IP address. Uses SQL LIKE operator for partial matching on the ip column. Example: '192.168.1' matches '192.168.1.100', '192.168.1.200', etc. Case-insensitive string matching.

createdAtFrom.description:
Start date for session creation time filter.

Filters sessions to include only those created on or after the specified date and time. Use this parameter combined with createdAtTo to define a date range for session creation. Expects ISO 8601 date-time format.
createdAtFrom.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for filtering sessions created on or after this timestamp. Applied as WHERE created_at >= createdAtFrom. Expects ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z').

createdAtTo.description:
End date for session creation time filter.

Filters sessions to include only those created on or before the specified date and time. Use this parameter combined with createdAtFrom to define a date range for session creation. Expects ISO 8601 date-time format.
createdAtTo.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for filtering sessions created on or before this timestamp. Applied as WHERE created_at <= createdAtTo. Expects ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z').

expiredAtFrom.description:
Start date for session expiration time filter.

Filters sessions to include only those that expire on or after the specified date and time. Useful for finding sessions that are still valid or will expire in the future. Expects ISO 8601 date-time format.
expiredAtFrom.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for filtering sessions that expire on or after this timestamp. Applied as WHERE expired_at >= expiredAtFrom. Expects ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z').

expiredAtTo.description:
End date for session expiration time filter.

Filters sessions to include only those that expire on or before the specified date and time. Useful for finding sessions that have already expired or will expire soon. Expects ISO 8601 date-time format.
expiredAtTo.x-autobe-specification: Query parameter for filtering sessions that expire on or before this timestamp. Applied as WHERE expired_at <= expiredAtTo. Expects ISO 8601 date-time format (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z').

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve. Page numbering starts at 1 (not 0). For example, page 1 returns the first set of results, page 2 returns the second set, and so on. Defaults to 1 if not specified.
page.x-autobe-specification: Pagination page number (1-indexed). Defaults to 1 if not provided. Used to calculate OFFSET in SQL: OFFSET = (page - 1) * limit. Must be >= 1.

limit.description:
Number of records per page.

Controls how many session records are returned in each page of results. Minimum is 1, maximum is 100. Defaults to 20 if not specified. Use a higher limit to retrieve more results per page, or a lower limit for smaller, more manageable result sets.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum number of records to return per page. Defaults to 20 if not provided. Valid range: 1 to 100. Used as LIMIT clause in SQL query. Values outside range are clamped to valid bounds.

sort.description:
Sort field and direction for result ordering.

Specifies how to sort the returned session records. Format is the field name followed by the sort direction (ASC for ascending, DESC for descending). Default sorting is by created_at in descending order (newest sessions first). Valid sort fields include id, actorType, actorId, ip, href, created_at, and expired_at.
sort.x-autobe-specification: Sort field and direction for result ordering. Format: 'fieldName direction' where direction is 'ASC' or 'DESC'. Default: 'created_at DESC'. Valid fields: id, actorType, actorId, ip, href, created_at, expired_at. Applied as ORDER BY clause in SQL.

IShoppingMallGuestSession.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering user sessions across all actor types in the shopping mall platform.

This request body enables administrators to search and filter session records from customers, sellers, administrators, and guests. You can filter by actor type, session status (active or expired), IP address, and date ranges for session creation and expiration times. Pagination parameters control how many results are returned and which page of results to retrieve.

All filter parameters are optional. If no filters are provided, the endpoint returns all sessions with default pagination (page 1, 20 records per page).
IShoppingMallGuestSession.IRequest.x-autobe-specification:
Request DTO for filtering and paginating user sessions across all actor types (customer, seller, administrator, guest). Used in PATCH /shoppingMall/guest/sessions endpoint.

Filtering logic:
- actorType: Determines which session table(s) to query. If not specified, queries all session tables with UNION ALL.
- status: Computed filter comparing expired_at with current time. 'active' means expired_at > NOW(), 'expired' means expired_at <= NOW().
- ip: Partial match filter using SQL LIKE operator on the ip column.
- createdAtFrom/createdAtTo: Date range filter using >= and <= operators on created_at column.
- expiredAtFrom/expiredAtTo: Date range filter using >= and <= operators on expired_at column.

Pagination:
- page: 1-indexed page number, defaults to 1
- limit: Records per page, defaults to 20, maximum 100
- sort: Sort field and direction, defaults to 'created_at DESC'

The query performs UNION ALL across filtered session tables (shopping_mall_customer_sessions, shopping_mall_seller_sessions, shopping_mall_administrator_sessions, shopping_mall_guest_sessions), then applies pagination and sorting.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this product snapshot variant option entry.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the option record, allowing precise identification and reference to individual option key-value pairs within product variant snapshots.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variant_options.id. UUID primary key uniquely identifying this option entry within the product snapshot variant.

key.description:
The option attribute name identifying the type of variant option.

This field contains standardized identifiers that categorize variant options. Common examples include 'Color', 'Size', 'Material', 'Pattern', and other product-specific attributes that distinguish variants within the same product.
key.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variant_options.key. String field containing the option attribute name such as 'Color', 'Size', or 'Material'.

value.description:
The specific option value representing the variant's selection for this attribute.

This field contains the actual option selections that distinguish variants from each other within the same product. For example, if the key is 'Color', the value might be 'Red', 'Blue', or 'Black'.
value.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variant_options.value. String field containing the specific option selection such as 'Red', 'Large', or 'Cotton'.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this option entry was created as part of the product snapshot.

This field records the exact moment when the product modification occurred and the snapshot was generated, capturing the precise time of the variant option state for audit trail purposes.
created_at.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variant_options.created_at. DateTime field with timezone indicating when this option entry was created as part of the product snapshot.

IShoppingMallProductSnapshotVariantOptio.description:
Individual option key-value pair captured in a product variant snapshot.

This immutable record represents a single attribute of a product variant at the time of product modification. Each option consists of a key (the attribute name such as 'Color', 'Size', 'Material') and a value (the specific selection such as 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton').

These option pairs are preserved permanently within product snapshots for audit compliance and dispute resolution, enabling accurate historical tracking of product configurations even after variants or products are deleted.
IShoppingMallProductSnapshotVariantOptio.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variant_options table. Fields: id (UUID primary key), key (option attribute name such as 'Color', 'Size', 'Material'), value (option selection such as 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton'), created_at (DateTime with timezone). The shopping_mall_product_snapshot_variant_id FK column and productSnapshotVariant relation are excluded as this subsidiary entity is always accessed through its parent IShoppingMallProductSnapshotVariant context, where the FK is implicitly resolved.
